plates.side_label: JUNE 1938 MAMMOTH CAVE (32 DAYS AT 54 °F / 120 FT DOWN): 28-HOUR CAVE SCHEDULE VS PERSISTENT ~24-HOUR TEMPERATURE CLOCK
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Mammoth Cave temperature and circadian rhythm chart from Nathaniel Kleitman (1939, Sleep and Wakefulness) compares the imposed 28-hour cave schedule (6 cycles per 7-day week at 54 °F / 12 °C in total darkness for 32 days) against Kleitman's persistent ~24-hour body-temperature oscillation (36.1–37.1 °C, peaking every 24 hours regardless of the cave clock).
